CitationText: Village Council meeting on 2017-04-19, agenda item 9 (Presentation): No formal action recorded. South Lee County Watershed Initiative Update - Josh Evans, J.R. Evans Engineering Village Manager Sarkozy explained that this related to the Village Stormwater Master Plan. Josh Evans provided introductory comments. In order for the exemption to be effective in 2016 taxes, the Village would need to adopt the additional senior homestead exemption. Village Attorney Burt Saunders noted that he has been in contact with the Village special tax counsel for guidance on the matter and he is expecting to hear from her on Monday, June 22. Discussion ensued regarding whether the exemption disappeared for this calendar year and the importance of clearing the matter up quickly. It was noted that this was a valuation exemption and related to Village ad velorem taxes only. It was suggested that Councilmembers bring up items at a Council meeting, and the item would go on a workshop agenda by consensus of four or more Councilmembers. ProjectTitle: ordinance following the first reading
Action: Councilmember Exrington moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2015-19 as amended, seconded by Councilmember Boesch. Discussion of the motion followed. Vice Mayor Levitan noted that Council was provided over…
CitationText: Village Council meeting on 2015-12-16, agenda item 7 (Ordinance): Councilmember Exrington moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2015-19 as amended, seconded by Councilmember Boesch. Discussion of the motion followed. Vice Mayor Levitan noted that Council was provided over 1,000 pages of documents relating to fracking; he focused on two in particular, the June 2015 report from New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, and the June 2015 Assessment of the Potential Impacts of Hydraulic Fracturing for Oil and Gas on Drinking Water Resources Executive Summary published by the Federal Environment Protection Agency. Vice Mayor Levitan also noted for the record that no one appeared before the Council that was against the ordinance, the Planning and Zoning Board found conclusively that the ordinance was consistent with the Comprehensive Plan, and voted to strongly recommend that Council (C) adopt the ordinance. He also referred to the preamble to the Estero Comprehensive Plan as well as Goal 19 Vision Statement. He stated that he believed that the ordinance was entirely consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and that the only way to protect quality of life in Estero was to ban the practice completely. Councilmember Errington conveyed appreciation to the Conservancy for all of the work involved and stated that water was the important issue. She agreed with Vice Mayor Levitan and noted that she has not had one person ask her to support fracking. Councilmember Boesch commented that the emphasis was on water, especially in this area. He suggested that the H2O Solutions report be included in the record. Attorney Saunders responded that all documents presented at the meeting would be part of the record, Mayor Batos stated that he was told that if the Council passed the ordinance and the Bill passed as written, the ordinance would be preempted; however, if the wording in the Bill was rewritten, the portion that would preempt the Village from controlling the zoning would be reinstated. He continued that he was not in favor of fracking; however, he wanted to be practical and put in laws that meant something. He stated that his responsibility was to represent the people; although he did not believe that the ordinance would accomplish anything, he would be in favor of the ordinance because he sensed that was what most people wanted. The motion was called and carried Source: https://estero-fl.gov/wp-content/uploads/library-ada/minutes/2015%20Minutes/Council/121615%20Regular%20Meeting%20Approved%20Minutes.pdf
